csp.policy.summary: Deploy an enforced Content-Security-Policy. Start from a nonce-based policy and roll it out with Report-Only first.
csp.policy.nginx:
# Replace $csp_nonce with a per-request nonce (ngx_http_sub_module or your app).
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'nonce-$csp_nonce' 'strict-dynamic' https: 'unsafe-inline'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'" always;
csp.policy.apache:
# mod_headers; generate the nonce in your application and expose it as %{CSP_NONCE}e
Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'nonce-%{CSP_NONCE}e' 'strict-dynamic' https: 'unsafe-inline'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'"
csp.policy.cdn:
# Cloudflare Transform Rule (Modify Response Header) -> Set static
# Header name:  Content-Security-Policy
# Value:        default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
# A nonce-based policy needs a Worker, since the value must change per request.
csp.policy.notes: Deploy as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first, collect violations for a release cycle, then switch the header name.

csp.default-src.summary: Add a restrictive default-src so unlisted fetch directives inherit a safe fallback.
csp.default-src.cdn: # Add `default-src 'self';` to the start of the CSP value in your Transform Rule.

csp.unsafe-inline.summary: Remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src and adopt per-request nonces with 'strict-dynamic'.
csp.unsafe-inline.apache: Header always set Content-Security-Policy "script-src 'nonce-%{CSP_NONCE}e' 'strict-dynamic' https: 'unsafe-inline'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'"
csp.unsafe-inline.cdn:
# Nonces cannot be produced by a static header rule. Use a Cloudflare Worker:
#   const nonce = crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g,'');
#   res.headers.set('Content-Security-Policy', `script-src 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic' https: 'unsafe-inline'`)
# and inject the same nonce into the HTML with HTMLRewriter.
csp.unsafe-inline.notes: 'unsafe-inline' is ignored by CSP3 browsers when a nonce is present, so keeping it is safe and helps old clients.

csp.unsafe-eval.summary: Remove 'unsafe-eval' and replace the eval-based code paths (templating engines, JSON parsing, dynamic imports).
csp.unsafe-eval.cdn: # Delete the `'unsafe-eval'` token from the CSP value in your Transform Rule or Worker.
csp.unsafe-eval.notes: Common sources are AngularJS's expression evaluator, older Vue builds with the runtime compiler, and Function() in analytics bundles.

csp.wildcard.summary: Replace wildcard, scheme-only and known-bypassable sources with an explicit host list, or move to 'strict-dynamic'.
csp.wildcard.apache: Header always set Content-Security-Policy "script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'"
csp.wildcard.cdn: # Replace `*`, `https:` and `data:` in script-src with the specific hosts you actually load scripts from.
csp.wildcard.notes: A host allowlist is only as strong as its weakest entry; 'strict-dynamic' removes the class of bypass entirely.

csp.object-src.summary: Set object-src 'none' to block plugin-based script execution.

csp.base-uri.summary: Set base-uri 'none' (or 'self') so an injected <base> tag cannot rewrite relative script URLs.
csp.base-uri.notes: base-uri does not fall back to default-src, so it must be listed explicitly.

csp.frame-ancestors.summary: Set frame-ancestors to 'none', or to the exact origins allowed to frame the page.
csp.frame-ancestors.notes: frame-ancestors supersedes X-Frame-Options and supports multiple origins, which X-Frame-Options never did.

csp.reporting.summary: Add a report-to group backed by a Reporting-Endpoints header alongside the legacy report-uri.
csp.reporting.nginx:
add_header Reporting-Endpoints 'csp-endpoint="https://example.com/csp-reports"' always;
add_header Content-Security-Policy "...; report-to csp-endpoint; report-uri https://example.com/csp-reports" always;
csp.reporting.apache:
Header always set Reporting-Endpoints "csp-endpoint=\"https://example.com/csp-reports\""
Header always set Content-Security-Policy "...; report-to csp-endpoint; report-uri https://example.com/csp-reports"
csp.reporting.cdn: # Add both a `Reporting-Endpoints` response header and a `report-to` directive in the CSP.
csp.reporting.notes: Keep report-uri for now: Safari still only understands that one.

hsts.summary: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a one-year max-age and includeSubDomains from the TLS vhost.
hsts.apache: Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
hsts.cdn:
# Cloudflare: SSL/TLS -> Edge Certificates -> HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) -> Enable
#   Max Age: 12 months, Apply to subdomains: On, Preload: On
hsts.notes: Only add `preload` once every subdomain is HTTPS-only: submission to hstspreload.org is slow to reverse.

xfo.summary: Send X-Frame-Options: DENY for legacy clients, and rely on CSP frame-ancestors for modern ones.
xfo.cdn: # Transform Rule -> Set static -> X-Frame-Options: DENY
xfo.notes: ALLOW-FROM is not supported anywhere; use CSP frame-ancestors when you need to allow specific origins.

nosniff.summary: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response.
nosniff.cdn: # Transform Rule -> Set static -> X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
nosniff.notes: Make sure Content-Type is correct for every response first, since nosniff makes the declared type binding.

referrer-policy.cdn: # Transform Rule -> Set static -> Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
referrer-policy.notes: strict-origin-when-cross-origin keeps the full URL for same-origin navigation and sends only the origin elsewhere.

permissions-policy.summary: Send Permissions-Policy denying the features the site does not use.
permissions-policy.nginx: add_header Permissions-Policy "accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()" always;
permissions-policy.apache: Header always set Permissions-Policy "accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()"
permissions-policy.caddy: header Permissions-Policy "accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()"
permissions-policy.cdn: # Transform Rule -> Set static -> Permissions-Policy: camera=(), geolocation=(), microphone=(), payment=()
permissions-policy.notes: An empty allowlist `()` denies the feature to the document and to every frame it embeds.

coop.summary: Send Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin to isolate the browsing context group.
coop.cdn: # Transform Rule -> Set static -> Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
coop.notes: Use same-origin-allow-popups if the site opens OAuth popups that need window.opener.

coep.summary: Send Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (or credentialless) to enable cross-origin isolation.
coep.cdn: # Transform Rule -> Set static -> Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp
coep.notes: This breaks third-party embeds that do not send CORP or CORS headers. Roll out behind Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy-Report-Only first.

corp.summary: Send Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin (or same-site) so other origins cannot embed the response.
corp.cdn: # Transform Rule -> Set static -> Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin
corp.notes: Use cross-origin for assets that are meant to be hotlinked, such as a public CDN bucket.

cors.summary: Never reflect an arbitrary Origin. Match against an explicit allowlist and only then echo it, and never combine a wildcard with credentials.
cors.apache:
SetEnvIf Origin "^https://(app|admin)\.example\.com$" CORS_ORIGIN=$0
Header always set Access-Control-Allow-Origin %{CORS_ORIGIN}e env=CORS_ORIGIN
Header always set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials "true" env=CORS_ORIGIN
Header always append Vary "Origin"
cors.notes: Also reject the literal string `null`: any sandboxed iframe can send it.

cookies.summary: Set Secure, HttpOnly and an explicit SameSite on every cookie, and use the __Host- prefix for session cookies.
cookies.nginx:
# nginx can only rewrite cookies it proxies:
proxy_cookie_flags ~ secure httponly samesite=lax;
# Preferably set the attributes in the application, e.g.:
#   Set-Cookie: __Host-session=...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
cookies.apache:
Header always edit Set-Cookie ^(.*)$ "$1; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax"
# Or, for the session cookie of a specific module:
#   php_value session.cookie_secure 1
#   php_value session.cookie_httponly 1
#   php_value session.cookie_samesite Lax
cookies.caddy:
# Caddy does not rewrite cookies; set the attributes in the upstream application:
#   Set-Cookie: __Host-session=...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
cookies.cdn:
# Cloudflare Transform Rule cannot safely rewrite Set-Cookie. Fix it in the origin application:
#   Set-Cookie: __Host-session=...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
cookies.notes: __Host- requires Secure, Path=/ and no Domain attribute, which pins the cookie to exactly one origin.

tls.versions.cdn: # Cloudflare: SSL/TLS -> Edge Certificates -> Minimum TLS Version -> TLS 1.2
tls.versions.notes: Check your client population before dropping TLS 1.0/1.1: it mostly affects Android 4.x and Windows XP era clients.

tls.ciphers.summary: Restrict TLS 1.2 to AEAD suites with forward secrecy and let the server pick the order.
tls.ciphers.apache:
SSLCipherSuite ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305
SSLHonorCipherOrder on
SSLOpenSSLConfCmd Curves X25519:prime256v1:secp384r1
tls.ciphers.cdn: # Cloudflare manages cipher selection at the edge; set Minimum TLS Version to 1.2 and leave the rest to the platform.
tls.ciphers.notes: The list above is the Mozilla "intermediate" profile minus the CBC suites.

tls.certificate.summary: Serve a certificate from a publicly trusted CA that covers the hostname, with the full intermediate chain, and automate renewal.
tls.certificate.apache:
SSLCertificateFile      /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem
SSLCertificateKeyFile   /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem
# Apache < 2.4.8 also needs SSLCertificateChainFile.
tls.certificate.cdn:
# Cloudflare: SSL/TLS -> Edge Certificates covers the edge.
# Use an Origin CA certificate on the origin and set the mode to Full (strict).
tls.certificate.notes: Verify the deployed chain with: openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com -showcerts

tls.ocsp.summary: Enable OCSP stapling so the handshake carries a fresh revocation proof.
tls.ocsp.caddy: # Caddy staples OCSP responses automatically for the certificates it manages.
tls.ocsp.cdn: # Cloudflare staples OCSP at the edge automatically; no configuration is required.
tls.ocsp.notes: Let's Encrypt has wound down its OCSP service; with a CA that no longer publishes OCSP this control is not applicable.

tls.extras.summary: Enable ALPN with HTTP/2, keep secure renegotiation on, and make sure TLS compression is disabled.
tls.extras.apache:
Protocols h2 http/1.1
SSLSessionCache "shmcb:/var/run/ssl_scache(512000)"
SSLCompression off
SSLInsecureRenegotiation off
tls.extras.cdn: # Cloudflare: Network -> HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (with QUIC) -> On
tls.extras.notes: TLS compression is off by default in every current OpenSSL build; if it is on, the build or configuration is unusually old.

redirect.summary: Redirect every plain-HTTP request to the same host over HTTPS with a single permanent redirect.
redirect.apache:
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName example.com
    Redirect permanent / https://example.com/
</VirtualHost>
# Or with mod_rewrite:
#   RewriteEngine On
#   RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off
#   RewriteRule ^ https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [R=301,L]
redirect.cdn: # Cloudflare: SSL/TLS -> Edge Certificates -> Always Use HTTPS -> On
redirect.notes: Redirect to the same host first and let that host redirect to the canonical name, otherwise the browser never records an HSTS entry for the original host.

mixed-content.summary: Change subresource URLs to https:// (or protocol-relative-free absolute HTTPS URLs) and add upgrade-insecure-requests as a backstop.
mixed-content.cdn:
# Cloudflare: SSL/TLS -> Edge Certificates -> Automatic HTTPS Rewrites -> On
# This rewrites http:// subresource URLs in HTML at the edge.
mixed-content.notes: upgrade-insecure-requests hides the problem rather than fixing it; correct the URLs in the templates as well.

security-txt.summary: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with at least Contact and Expires, served over HTTPS as text/plain.
security-txt.apache:
# Place the file at DOCUMENT_ROOT/.well-known/security.txt and force its type:
<Files "security.txt">
    ForceType text/plain
</Files>
security-txt.cdn:
# Cloudflare Pages/Workers: serve a static /.well-known/security.txt with Content-Type: text/plain,
# or use a Worker that returns the file contents for that path.
security-txt.notes: Sign the file with PGP and link the signature from the Canonical field if you publish a key.

http-methods.summary: Disable TRACE and restrict the methods the server will act on to those the application needs.
http-methods.apache:
TraceEnable off
<LimitExcept GET HEAD POST OPTIONS>
    Require all denied
</LimitExcept>
http-methods.caddy:
@bad_method not method GET HEAD POST PUT PATCH DELETE OPTIONS
respond @bad_method 405
http-methods.cdn:
# Cloudflare WAF custom rule:
#   Expression: (http.request.method in {"TRACE" "TRACK" "CONNECT"})
#   Action:     Block

info-headers.summary: Suppress headers that advertise software versions.
info-headers.apache:
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
Header always unset X-Powered-By
Header always unset X-AspNet-Version
Header always unset X-AspNetMvc-Version
Header always unset X-Generator
# PHP: expose_php = Off in php.ini
info-headers.cdn:
# Cloudflare Transform Rule (Modify Response Header) -> Remove:
#   X-Powered-By, X-AspNet-Version, X-AspNetMvc-Version, X-Generator
info-headers.notes: This is obscurity, not security. Do it because it is free, not because it protects anything on its own.

legacy-headers.summary: Remove withdrawn security headers: X-XSS-Protection, Public-Key-Pins and Expect-CT.
legacy-headers.apache:
Header always unset X-XSS-Protection
Header always unset Public-Key-Pins
Header always unset Public-Key-Pins-Report-Only
Header always unset Expect-CT
legacy-headers.cdn:
# Cloudflare Transform Rule (Modify Response Header) -> Remove:
#   X-XSS-Protection, Public-Key-Pins, Expect-CT
legacy-headers.notes: If a compliance checklist insists on X-XSS-Protection, send the value 0, which disables the removed auditor rather than enabling it.
